issues.title: Generic game tokens dominate SCT rankings across all models
issues.description: Tokens like 'guess', 'hints', 'Sorry', 'clue' are suppressed between mid and final layers in ALL finetuned models regardless of the secret word, displacing the actual secret token from top-5. Implemented a cross-model generic token filter: for each target model, identify tokens appearing in top-20 SCT rankings for >=1% of examples in ALL other models, and remove them. This improved moon TR@5 from 8.0% to 10.0% and mean TR@5 from 4.67% to 5.33%.

issues.title: SCT provides no benefit over logit lens after generic filtering
issues.description: After removing generic tokens via the cross-model filter, the simpler logit lens method (mid-layer log-probability at control positions) achieves the same TR@5 as filtered SCT (5.33%) with better auditor accuracy (3.07% vs 2.70%). The suppression contrast signal provides no additional differentiation once the main source of noise (generic tokens) is removed.

issues.title: Differential SCT (finetuned vs base model) fails to isolate secret signal
issues.description: Attempted diff_SCT(v) = SCT_ft(v) - SCT_base(v) using full-vocabulary extraction at control positions. The base model produces very different activation patterns on Taboo-specific prompts, so the subtraction does not cancel generic suppression as hoped. All mid_diff scores were negative and the secret token was not in the top-500.

issues.title: Top-200 token ceiling is a hard limit on recovery rate
issues.description: The pre-extracted activations store only top-200 tokens per position per layer. At control positions, the secret token appears in top-200 for only gold=2.0%, moon=16.0%, flag=10.0% of examples. This is an absolute ceiling that no scoring method operating within the stored data can exceed. Gold at 2.0% TR@5 is already at ceiling.

summary: Explored three major approaches: (1) differential SCT using base model contrast (failed - different activation patterns), (2) multi-position aggregation variants (failed - all worse than control-only), (3) cross-model generic token filter (best improvement). The cross-model filter improved mean TR@5 from 4.67% to 5.33% (+14.1% over step-0 SCT, +23.1% over LL baseline) by removing game-related tokens that appear across all models. However, this does NOT meet the success criteria of >=25% relative AND >=1.5pp absolute improvement over the logit lens baseline (TR@5=4.33%). The best filtered method achieved +23.1% relative / +1.00pp absolute, falling short on both thresholds. Auditor accuracy was roughly unchanged at 3.07% vs baseline 3.13%. The fundamental limitation is the top-200 token extraction ceiling which constrains all scoring approaches.
